class AcMeasure
#include <ac_measure.h>

Manages AC measurement operations over I2C, providing access to voltage, current, power, and energy data.

The AcMeasure class facilitates interaction with an AC measurement device via I2C communication. It supports reading raw and converted electrical parameters such as voltage, current, power, apparent power, power factor, and energy consumption. Additionally, it allows configuration of calibration factors and I2C address.

Public Functions

ac_measure_error_t begin(void)

Initializes the AC measurement device by checking I2C connectivity.

This function verifies the presence of the device at the specified I2C address. It must be called before any other operations to ensure proper communication.

Attention

Ensure the device is powered and correctly connected to the I2C bus.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • UNIT_AC_MEASURE_OK: Success

  • UNIT_AC_MEASURE_ERR_I2C: I2C communication failure

uint8_t getFirmwareVersion(void)

Retrieves the firmware version of the AC measurement device.

Reads the firmware version from the device’s firmware version register.

Attention

Requires successful initialization via begin().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

uint8_t The firmware version.

Checks the readiness status of the AC measurement device.

Queries the device to determine if it is ready to provide measurement data.

Attention

Requires successful initialization via begin().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

uint8_t The readiness status (typically 0 or 1).

class BMP280
#include <bmp280.h>

Manages environmental measurements using the BMP280 sensor, providing access to pressure, temperature, and altitude data.

The BMP280 class facilitates interaction with the BMP280 environmental sensor over I2C. It supports reading pressure, temperature, and altitude, with calibration and configuration options for sampling, filtering, and operating modes. The class stores converted sensor values for easy access and provides utility functions for sea level pressure and water boiling point calculations.

Public Functions

bmp280_error_t begin()

Initializes the BMP280 sensor.

Verifies I2C connectivity, reads calibration coefficients, and sets default sampling parameters.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is powered and connected to the I2C bus before calling.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • BMP280_OK: Success

  • BMP280_ERR_I2C: I2C communication failure

bmp280_error_t update()

Updates all sensor measurements.

Reads temperature, pressure, and altitude in sequence, storing results in the internal sensor array.

Attention

Requires successful initialization via begin().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • BMP280_OK: Success

bmp280_error_t reset(void)

Resets the BMP280 sensor.

Sends a soft reset command to the sensor, restoring it to its power-on state.

Attention

Requires successful initialization via begin(). May disrupt ongoing measurements.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • BMP280_OK: Success

uint8_t getStatus(void)

Reads the current status of the BMP280 sensor.

Retrieves the sensor’s status register to check measurement and image update status.

Attention

Requires successful initialization via begin().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

uint8_t The status register value.

bmp280_error_t readPressure()

Reads the pressure from the BMP280 sensor.

Retrieves raw pressure data, applies calibration coefficients, and stores the result in the internal sensor array.

Attention

Requires temperature to be read first to set the t_fine variable. Ensure successful initialization via begin().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • BMP280_OK: Success

  • BMP280_ERR_DIV_ZERO: Division by zero error during calculation

bmp280_error_t readTemperature()

Reads the temperature from the BMP280 sensor.

Retrieves raw temperature data, applies calibration coefficients, and stores the result in the internal sensor array.

Attention

Requires successful initialization via begin().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • BMP280_OK: Success

bmp280_error_t readAltitude()

Calculates the altitude based on pressure data.

Uses the current pressure and sea level pressure to compute altitude, storing the result in the internal sensor array.

Attention

Requires a prior call to readPressure() and valid sea level pressure.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • BMP280_OK: Success

float getPressure()

Retrieves the pressure value.

Returns the previously read pressure value stored in the internal sensor array, in Pascals.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to readPressure() or update().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

float The pressure value in Pascals.

float getTemperature()

Retrieves the temperature value.

Returns the previously read temperature value stored in the internal sensor array, in degrees Celsius.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to readTemperature() or update().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

float The temperature value in °C.

float getAltitude()

Retrieves the altitude value.

Returns the previously calculated altitude value stored in the internal sensor array, in meters.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to readAltitude() or update().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

float The altitude value in meters.

float seaLevelForAltitude(float altitude, float atmospheric)

Calculates sea level pressure for a given altitude and atmospheric pressure.

Computes the equivalent sea level pressure based on the provided altitude and measured atmospheric pressure.

Attention

The provided values should be valid and within reasonable ranges.

Parameters:

  • altitude – [in] The altitude in meters.

  • atmospheric – [in] The measured atmospheric pressure in Pascals.

Returns:

float The calculated sea level pressure in hPa.

void setSeaLevelPressure(float pressure)

Sets the sea level pressure for altitude calculations.

Updates the internal sea level pressure value used for altitude computations.

Attention

The provided pressure should be a valid value (typically around 1013.25 hPa).

Parameters:

pressure – [in] The sea level pressure in hPa.

float waterBoilingPoint(float pressure)

Calculates the water boiling point based on pressure.

Computes the boiling point of water at the given atmospheric pressure using a logarithmic formula.

Parameters:

pressure – [in] The atmospheric pressure in hPa.

Returns:

None –

Returns:

  • true: Measurement completed successfully

class ButtonHandler
#include <button.h>

Manages button presses, handling debouncing, click detection, and hold events.

The ButtonHandler class provides functionality for processing button interactions, including single-click, double-click, and hold events. It utilizes a finite state machine (FSM) to ensure reliable event detection, minimizing issues related to button bouncing.

Parameters:

  • isActiveLow – [in] True if the button’s active state is LOW.

  • usePullup – [in] True to enable internal pull-up resistor.

Returns:

  • BUTTON_ERR_INVALID_PARAM: Invalid pin number.

class DHT20
#include <dht20.h>

Manages communication with the DHT20 temperature and humidity sensor.

The DHT20 class provides an interface for interacting with the DHT20 sensor using I2C communication. It allows users to initialize the sensor, read temperature and humidity data, and handle sensor status.

Public Functions

DHT20()
dht20_error_t begin()

Initializes the DHT20 sensor.

This function initializes the DHT20 sensor by waiting for a brief period after power-on and then resetting the sensor.

Attention

Ensure that the sensor is correctly connected and powered on before calling this function. This function includes a 100ms delay to allow the sensor to stabilize after power-on.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • DHT20_OK: Initialization success.

dht20_error_t readTempAndHumidity()

Reads temperature and humidity data from the DHT20 sensor.

This function attempts to read temperature and humidity data from the DHT20 sensor. It retries the operation multiple times if the sensor is not ready or data is not available. The raw sensor values are then converted to floating-point temperature and humidity values.

Attention

Ensure that the sensor is correctly connected and that I2C communication is functioning. This function may block for short periods while waiting for the sensor to be ready and for data to be available.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • DHT20_OK: Success

  • DHT20_TIMEOUT: Timeout, the sensor is not ready or data is not available after multiple attempts.

float getHumidity()

Get humidity data from the DHT20 sensor.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

int The humidity data

float getTemperature()

Get temperature data from the DHT20 sensor.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

int The temperature data

Private Functions

dht20_error_t readTargetData(uint32_t *data)

Reads temperature and humidity data from the DHT20 sensor.

This function reads a 6-byte buffer from the DHT20 sensor, where the first byte is the status register, and the remaining 5 bytes contain temperature and humidity data. It processes these bytes to extract the humidity and temperature values.

Attention

Ensure that the sensor is properly connected and that the I2C communication is functioning. The function waits for 80 milliseconds for the measurement to complete, which might block other operations during this time.

Parameters:

  • None – [in]

  • data – [out] Pointer to a buffer where the temperature and humidity data will be stored.

    • data[HUMIDITY_INDEX] will hold the processed humidity data.

    • data[TEMPERATURE_INDEX] will hold the processed temperature data.

Returns:

  • DHT20_OK: Success

  • DHT20_ERR_I2C_WRITE: Error writing to the I2C bus

  • DHT20_ERR_I2C_READ: Error reading from the I2C bus

  • DHT20_ERR: Sensor is still busy or not ready

int readStatus()

Reads the status register of the DHT20 sensor.

This function reads the status register byte from the DHT20 sensor and checks specific bits to determine the status of the sensor.

Attention

Ensure that the sensor is correctly connected and that I2C communication is functioning. This function may print an error message if the byte read operation fails.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • 1: If (status byte & 0x18) == 0x18

  • 0: If (status byte & 0x18) != 0x18

int reset()

Resets the DHT20 sensor.

This function resets the sensor by writing to specific registers. The logic for resetting the sensor is adapted from another source with modifications. The function checks the sensor status and attempts to reset the registers. Use with care.

Attention

Use with care.

Note

See datasheet 7.4 Sensor Reading Process, point 1.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • 3: OK, all registers reset successfully.

  • 0, 1, 2: Error, not all registers reset.

  • 255: No reset needed.

bool _resetRegister(uint8_t reg)

Resets a specific register of the DHT20 sensor.

This function writes to a specific register to reset it. The logic is based on demo code provided by AOSONG.

Attention

Ensure that the I2C communication is functioning correctly.

Parameters:

reg – [in] The register address to reset.

Returns:

  • true: Register reset successfully.

  • false: Failed to reset the register.

class EsSoil7n1
#include <es_soil_7n1.h>

Manages soil sensor measurements via RS485 Modbus, providing access to pH, moisture, temperature, conductivity, and nutrient levels.

The EsSoil7n1 class facilitates interaction with a 7-in-1 soil sensor over an RS485 Modbus interface. It supports reading soil parameters including pH, moisture, temperature, conductivity, nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. The class uses Modbus commands to retrieve data and stores converted values for easy access.

Public Functions

es_soil_7n1_error_t readSoilPh()

Reads soil pH value.

This function sends a specific command over RS485 to read the soil’s pH level and processes the sensor’s response to extract and store the pH value.

Attention

Ensure that the RS485 communication and sensor connections are functional before calling this function.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • ES_SOIL_7N1_OK: pH reading was successful.

  • ES_SOIL_7N1_ERR: Error occurred during communication or response validation.

void beginRequest()

Start a more complex request. Use this when you need to send additional headers in the request, but you will also need to call endRequest() when you are finished.

void endRequest()

End a more complex request. Use this when you need to have sent additional headers in the request, but you will also need to call beginRequest() at the start.

void beginBody()

Start the body of a more complex request. Use this when you need to send the body after additional headers in the request, but can optionally call endRequest() when you are finished.

void sendHeader(const char *aHeader)

Send an additional header line. This can only be called in between the calls to beginRequest and endRequest.

Parameters:

aHeader – Header line to send, in its entirety (but without the trailing CRLF. E.g. “Authorization: Basic YQDDCAIGES”

inline void sendHeader(const String &aHeader)
void sendHeader(const char *aHeaderName, const char *aHeaderValue)

Send an additional header line. This is an alternate form of sendHeader() which takes the header name and content as separate strings. The call will add the “: “ to separate the header, so for example, to send a XXXXXX header call sendHeader(“XXXXX”, “Something”)

Parameters:

  • aHeaderName – Type of header being sent

  • aHeaderValue – Value for that header

inline void sendHeader(const String &aHeaderName, const String &aHeaderValue)

Send an additional header line. This is an alternate form of sendHeader() which takes the header name and content separately but where the value is provided as an integer. The call will add the “: “ to separate the header, so for example, to send a XXXXXX header call sendHeader(“XXXXX”, 123)

Parameters:

  • aHeaderName – Type of header being sent

  • aHeaderValue – Value for that header

int responseStatusCode()

Get the HTTP status code contained in the response. For example, 200 for successful request, 404 for file not found, etc.

bool headerAvailable()

Check if a header is available to be read. Use readHeaderName() to read header name, and readHeaderValue() to read the header value MUST be called after responseStatusCode() and before contentLength()

String readHeaderName()

Read the name of the current response header. Returns empty string if a header is not available.

String readHeaderValue()

Read the value of the current response header. Returns empty string if a header is not available.

int readHeader()

Read the next character of the response headers. This functions in the same way as read() but to be used when reading through the headers. Check whether or not the end of the headers has been reached by calling endOfHeadersReached(), although after that point this will still return data as read() would, but slightly less efficiently MUST be called after responseStatusCode() and before contentLength()

Returns:

The next character of the response headers

int skipResponseHeaders()

Skip any response headers to get to the body. Use this if you don’t want to do any special processing of the headers returned in the response. You can also use it after you’ve found all of the headers you’re interested in, and just want to get on with processing the body. MUST be called after responseStatusCode()

Returns:

HTTP_SUCCESS if successful, else an error code

bool endOfHeadersReached()

Test whether all of the response headers have been consumed.

Returns:

true if we are now processing the response body, else false

bool endOfBodyReached()

Test whether the end of the body has been reached. Only works if the Content-Length header was returned by the server

Returns:

true if we are now at the end of the body, else false

inline virtual bool endOfStream()
inline virtual bool completed()
long contentLength()

Return the length of the body. Also skips response headers if they have not been read already MUST be called after responseStatusCode()

Returns:

Length of the body, in bytes, or kNoContentLengthHeader if no Content-Length header was returned by the server

true if response body is chunked, false otherwise

response body of request as a String

class LCD_I2C : public Print

Public Functions

inline LCD_I2C(uint8_t address, uint8_t columns = 16, uint8_t rows = 2)
void begin(TwoWire *wire)

function begin

Parameters:

beginWire – if true start I²C wire

void backlight()

switch backlight on

void backlightOff()

switch backlight off

void clear()

Clears the LCD screen and positions the cursor in the upper-left corner.

void home()

Positions the cursor in the upper-left of the LCD. That is, use that location in outputting subsequent text to the display. To also clear the display, use the clear() function instead.

void leftToRight()

Set the direction for text written to the LCD to left-to-right, the default. This means that subsequent characters written to the display will go from left to right, but does not affect previously-output text.

void rightToLeft()

Set the direction for text written to the LCD to right-to-left (the default is left-to-right). This means that subsequent characters written to the display will go from right to left, but does not affect previously-output text.

void autoscroll()

set autoscroll on. Each character is printed on the same location on the LCD. Depending on the current text direction, autoscroll moves each character to the left when left => right is set. Or moves each character to the right when right => left is set.

void autoscrollOff()

Set autoscroll off. Moves the cursor one step when adding a character.

void display()

Turns on the LCD display, after it’s been turned off with noDisplay(). This will restore the text (and cursor) that was on the display.

void displayOff()

Turns off the LCD display, without losing the text currently shown on it.

void cursor()

Shows the cursor.

void cursorOff()

Hides the cursor.

void blink()

Display the blinking LCD cursor. If used in combination with the cursor() function, the result will depend on the particular display.

void blinkOff()

Turns off the blinking LCD cursor.

void scrollDisplayLeft()

Scrolls the contents of the display (text and cursor) one space to the left.

void scrollDisplayRight()

Scrolls the contents of the display (text and cursor) one space to the right.

void createChar(uint8_t memory_location, uint8_t charmap[])

Create a custom character (glyph) for use on the LCD. Up to eight characters of 5x8 pixels are supported (numbered 0 to 7). The appearance of each custom character is specified by an array of eight bytes, one for each row. The five least significant bits of each byte determine the pixels in that row. To display a custom character on the screen, write() its number.

Parameters:

  • memory_location – memory location where char is saved

  • charmap – defined character map

Set Cursor to position defined by column and row.

class LightSensor
#include <light_sensor.h>

Manages light intensity measurements using an analog light sensor.

The LightSensor class provides functionality for reading and processing light intensity data from an analog light sensor connected to a specified Arduino pin. It supports raw analog readings with 12-bit ADC resolution, mapped values, threshold detection, averaging, and callback triggering for threshold events.

Public Functions

LightSensor(int pin)

Constructor to initialize the LightSensor with a specified pin.

Configures the LightSensor to use the provided analog pin for reading light intensity and sets the ADC resolution to 12 bits.

Attention

Ensure the pin is a valid analog input pin on the microcontroller.

Parameters:

pin – [in] The analog pin connected to the light sensor.

light_sensor_error_t read()

Reads the analog value from the light sensor.

Uses the bspGpioAnalogRead function to retrieve the raw 12-bit analog value (0–4095) from the sensor and computes a percentage value (0–100), storing both internally.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is properly connected to the specified pin.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • LIGHT_SENSOR_OK: Success

  • LIGHT_SENSOR_ERR: Reading error

int readAndMap(int minValue, int maxValue)

Reads and maps the sensor value to a specified range.

Reads the raw analog value from the sensor and maps it to a user-defined range (e.g., 0–100) using linear scaling.

Attention

Ensure minValue is less than maxValue and the sensor is connected.

Parameters:

  • minValue – [in] Minimum value of the output range.

  • maxValue – [in] Maximum value of the output range.

Returns:

int The mapped sensor value within the specified range.

bool isAboveThreshold(int threshold)

Checks if the light intensity exceeds a threshold.

Compares the current raw sensor value against a specified threshold to determine if the light intensity is above it.

Attention

Requires a prior call to read() to update the sensor value.

Parameters:

threshold – [in] The threshold value for light intensity (0–4095).

Returns:

bool true if the light intensity is above the threshold, false otherwise.

int getLightValue()

Retrieves the raw analog light sensor value.

Returns the most recent raw 12-bit analog value (0–4095) read from the sensor.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to read().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

int The raw analog sensor value.

int getLightValuePercentage()

Retrieves the light intensity as a percentage.

Returns the internally stored percentage value (0–100) computed from the raw analog sensor value.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to read().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

int The light intensity as a percentage.

int getAverageReading(int samples = 10)

Computes the average sensor reading over multiple samples.

Takes multiple readings from the sensor with a 10ms delay between each and returns their average to reduce noise.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is connected and samples is a positive integer.

Parameters:

samples – [in] Number of samples to average (default: 10).

Returns:

int The averaged raw sensor value.

light_sensor_error_t onThresholdCross(int threshold, void (*callback)())

Sets a callback function for threshold-crossing events.

Configures a callback function to be triggered when the light intensity crosses the specified threshold, invoking the callback if the threshold is currently exceeded.

Attention

The callback function must be defined, have no parameters, and no return value. Requires a prior call to read() for accurate threshold detection.

Parameters:

  • threshold – [in] The threshold value for triggering the callback (0–4095).

  • callback – [in] The function to call when the threshold is crossed.

Returns:

  • LIGHT_SENSOR_OK: Success

  • LIGHT_SENSOR_ERR: Invalid callback or configuration error

Private Members

int _pin
uint32_t sensorValue[2]

SIG pin of the Light Sensor

void (*_callback)() = nullptr

Value from the sensor

class MiniFan
#include <mini_fan.h>

Manages operations of a mini fan module, providing control over speed and state.

The MiniFan class facilitates interaction with a mini fan module connected to an Arduino pin. It supports setting the fan speed via PWM, toggling the fan state, and retrieving the current speed as a raw PWM value or percentage. The class maintains the fan’s state internally for consistent control.

Public Functions

MiniFan(int pin)

Constructor to initialize the MiniFan with a specified pin.

Configures the MiniFan to use the provided PWM-capable pin as an output for controlling the fan.

Attention

Ensure the pin is PWM-capable and properly connected to the fan.

Parameters:

pin – [in] The pin number connected to the fan’s control signal.

void setFanSpeed(int speed)

Sets the fan speed using a PWM value.

Writes a PWM value to the control pin to set the fan speed and updates the internal speed and state.

Attention

Ensure the speed is within the valid range (0–255).

Parameters:

speed – [in] The fan speed as a PWM value (0–255).

void setFanSpeedPercentage(int percentage)

Sets the fan speed as a percentage.

Converts the percentage to a PWM value, writes it to the control pin, and updates the internal speed and state.

Attention

Ensure the percentage is within the valid range (0–100).

Parameters:

percentage – [in] The fan speed as a percentage (0–100%).

int getFanSpeed()

Retrieves the current fan speed.

Returns the current fan speed as a PWM value stored internally.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

int The current fan speed as a PWM value (0–255).

int getFanSpeedPercentage()

Retrieves the current fan speed as a percentage.

Returns the current fan speed as a percentage stored internally.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

int The current fan speed as a percentage (0–100%).

void toggleFan()

Toggles the fan state between ON and OFF.

Switches the fan state: if ON, turns it OFF by setting the PWM to 0; if OFF, turns it ON by restoring the previous speed or defaulting to maximum (PWM 255, 100%) if no prior speed was set.

Attention

The fan speed is preserved when turning OFF and restored when turning ON, unless no prior speed was set, in which case maximum speed is used.

Parameters:

None –

bool isFanRunning()

Checks if the fan is currently running.

Returns the current state of the fan based on the internally stored status.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

bool true if the fan is running, false otherwise.

Private Members

int _pin
int _speed[2]

SIG pin of the Mini Fan

bool status

Speed of the fan Status of the fan (ON/OFF)

class PIRSensor
#include <pir_sensor.h>

Manages motion detection using a PIR sensor module.

The PIRSensor class provides functionality for detecting motion via a Passive Infrared (PIR) sensor connected to an Arduino pin. It supports reading motion status, setting debounce times, detecting continuous motion, managing callbacks for motion events, and adjusting sensitivity.

Public Functions

PIRSensor(uint8_t pin)

Constructor to initialize the PIR sensor with a specified pin.

Configures the specified pin as a digital input for reading the PIR sensor output.

Attention

Ensure the pin is a valid digital input pin on the microcontroller.

Parameters:

pin – [in] The digital pin connected to the PIR sensor output.

void read()

Reads the current motion status from the PIR sensor.

Checks the sensor’s digital output, applies debouncing, and updates the internal motion status. Triggers the callback function if motion is detected and a callback is set.

Attention

Ensure setDebounceTime() is called if debouncing is needed to avoid false triggers.

Parameters:

None –

uint8_t getStatus()

Retrieves the current motion status.

Returns the latest motion status from the internal state.

Attention

Requires a prior call to read() to update the status.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

uint8_t

  • 1: Motion detected

  • 0: No motion detected

pir_sensor_error_t setDebounceTime(unsigned long debounceTime)

Sets the debounce time to avoid false motion triggers.

Configures the minimum time between consecutive motion detections to filter out noise.

Attention

Should be called before read() if debouncing is required.

Parameters:

debounceTime – [in] The debounce time in milliseconds.

Returns:

  • PIR_SENSOR_OK: Success

  • PIR_SENSOR_ERR: Invalid debounce time

int isMotionContinuous(unsigned long duration)

Checks if motion is continuously detected for a specified duration.

Monitors the sensor output for the specified duration to confirm continuous motion.

Attention

This function blocks until the duration expires or motion ceases.

Parameters:

duration – [in] The duration in milliseconds to check for continuous motion.

Returns:

  • 1: Motion detected continuously for the duration

  • 0: No continuous motion detected

unsigned long getLastMotionTime()

Retrieves the timestamp of the last motion detection.

Returns the time (in milliseconds) when motion was last detected.

Attention

Requires a prior call to read() to update the motion timestamp.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

unsigned long The timestamp (in milliseconds) of the last motion detection.

pir_sensor_error_t setMotionCallback(void (*callback)())

Enables a callback function for motion detection events.

Configures a callback function to be invoked when motion is detected during a read() call.

Attention

The callback must be defined and have no parameters or return value.

Parameters:

callback – [in] The function to call when motion is detected (signature: void callback()).

Returns:

  • PIR_SENSOR_OK: Success

  • PIR_SENSOR_ERR: Invalid callback

pir_sensor_error_t disableMotionCallback()

Disables the motion detection callback.

Clears the callback function, preventing it from being triggered on motion detection.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • PIR_SENSOR_OK: Success

pir_sensor_error_t setSensitivity(int level)

Sets the sensitivity of the PIR sensor.

Adjusts the debounce time to simulate sensitivity levels: low (1000ms), medium (500ms), or high (200ms).

Attention

Higher sensitivity reduces debounce time, increasing responsiveness but potentially false triggers.

Parameters:

level – [in] The sensitivity level (1: Low, 2: Medium, 3: High).

Returns:

  • PIR_SENSOR_OK: Success

  • PIR_SENSOR_ERR: Invalid sensitivity level

int reset()

Resets the PIR sensor to default settings.

Clears the motion status, last motion timestamp, debounce time, and callback function.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • PIR_SENSOR_OK: Success

Private Members

uint8_t _pin

Pin connected to the PIR sensor output.

uint8_t status
unsigned long _lastMotionTime

Status of the detection Timestamp of the last detected motion.

unsigned long _debounceTime

Debounce time in milliseconds.

void (*_motionCallback)()

Callback function for motion detection.

class SHT3X
#include <sht3x.h>

Manages temperature and humidity measurements using the SHT3X sensor.

The SHT3X class provides functionality for interfacing with the SHT3X temperature and humidity sensor over an I2C interface. It supports initializing the sensor, updating temperature and humidity readings, and retrieving values in Celsius, Fahrenheit, or percentage humidity. The class stores sensor data internally for efficient access.

Public Functions

sht3x_error_t begin(uint8_t i2c_addr = SHT3X_I2C_ADDR_DEFAULT)

Initializes the SHT3X sensor.

Configures the sensor with the specified I2C address and checks for its presence on the I2C bus.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is powered and connected to the I2C bus before calling.

Parameters:

i2c_addr – [in] The I2C address of the sensor (default: SHT3X_I2C_ADDR_DEFAULT, 0x44).

Returns:

  • SHT3X_OK: Sensor detected and initialized successfully

  • SHT3X_ERR_I2C: Sensor not found or I2C communication error

sht3x_error_t update(void)

Updates temperature and humidity readings from the SHT3X sensor.

Sends a high-repeatability measurement command with clock stretching enabled, reads the raw data, and converts it to temperature (Celsius) and humidity (percentage) values, storing them internally.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is initialized with begin() and connected to the I2C bus. The function includes delays (200ms + 50ms) for measurement completion.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • SHT3X_OK: Measurement successful

float getHumidity()

Retrieves the last measured humidity.

Returns the most recent humidity reading stored internally, as a percentage.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to update().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

float The relative humidity percentage (RH).

float getTemperatureCelcius()

Retrieves the last measured temperature in Celsius.

Returns the most recent temperature reading stored internally, in degrees Celsius.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to update().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

float The temperature in degrees Celsius.

float getTemperatureFahrenheit()

Retrieves the last measured temperature in Fahrenheit.

Converts the most recent temperature reading stored internally from Celsius to Fahrenheit.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to update().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

float The temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.

Private Members

float sensorValues[2] = {0}
uint8_t _addr
class SHT4X
#include <sht4x.h>

Manages temperature and humidity measurements using the SHT4X sensor.

The SHT4X class facilitates interaction with the SHT4X temperature and humidity sensor over an I2C interface. It supports initializing the sensor, configuring measurement precision and heater settings, and retrieving temperature and humidity data. The class stores sensor values internally for easy access.

Public Functions

sht4x_error_t begin()

Initializes the SHT4X sensor.

Checks for the presence of the SHT4X sensor on the I2C bus at address 0x44.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is powered and connected to the I2C bus before calling.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • SHT4X_OK: Sensor detected and initialized successfully

  • SHT4X_ERR_I2C: Sensor not found or I2C communication error

sht4x_error_t update(void)

Updates temperature and humidity readings from the SHT4X sensor.

Sends a measurement command based on the configured precision and heater settings, waits for the conversion time, reads the data, verifies the checksum, and updates internal temperature and humidity values.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is initialized with begin() and properly connected to the I2C bus.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • SHT4X_OK: Measurement successful

  • SHT4X_ERR_CHECKSUM: Checksum mismatch indicating data corruption

void setPrecision(sht4x_precision_t prec)

Sets the measurement precision of the SHT4X sensor.

Configures the sensor to use high, medium, or low precision for measurements, affecting accuracy and conversion time.

Attention

Changes take effect on the next update() call.

Parameters:

prec – [in] Desired precision setting (SHT4X_HIGH_PRECISION, SHT4X_MED_PRECISION, or SHT4X_LOW_PRECISION).

sht4x_precision_t getPrecision(void)

Retrieves the current measurement precision setting.

Returns the currently configured precision level of the sensor.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

sht4x_precision_t The current precision setting.

void setHeater(sht4x_heater_t heat)

Sets the heater mode of the SHT4X sensor.

Configures the built-in heater to one of several power levels and durations, or disables it.

Attention

Heater settings affect power consumption and measurement duration. Changes take effect on the next update() call.

Parameters:

heat – [in] Desired heater mode (e.g., SHT4X_NO_HEATER, SHT4X_HIGH_HEATER_1S).

sht4x_heater_t getHeater(void)

Retrieves the current heater mode setting.

Returns the currently configured heater mode of the sensor.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

sht4x_heater_t The current heater mode setting.

float getTemperature()

Retrieves the last measured temperature.

Returns the most recent temperature reading stored internally, in degrees Celsius.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to update().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

float The temperature in degrees Celsius.

float getHumidity()

Retrieves the last measured humidity.

Returns the most recent relative humidity reading stored internally, constrained to 0–100%.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to update().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

float The relative humidity percentage (RH).

class SoilMoisture
#include <soil_moisture.h>

Manages soil moisture measurements using an analog soil moisture sensor.

The SoilMoisture class provides functionality for reading and processing soil moisture data from an analog sensor connected to an Arduino pin. It supports raw analog readings, mapped values, threshold detection, averaging, and callback triggering for threshold events.

Public Functions

SoilMoisture(int pin)

Constructor to initialize the SoilMoisture sensor with a specified pin.

Configures the SoilMoisture sensor to use the provided analog pin for reading moisture levels.

Attention

Ensure the pin is a valid analog input pin on the microcontroller.

Parameters:

pin – [in] The analog pin connected to the soil moisture sensor.

void read()

Reads the analog value from the soil moisture sensor.

Uses the bspGpioAnalogRead function to retrieve the raw 10-bit analog value (0–1023) from the sensor and computes a percentage value (0–100), storing both internally.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is properly connected to the specified pin.

Parameters:

None –

uint32_t readAndMap(int minValue, int maxValue)

Reads and maps the sensor value to a specified range.

Reads the raw analog value from the sensor and maps it to a user-defined range (e.g., 0–100) using linear scaling.

Attention

Ensure minValue is less than maxValue and the sensor is connected.

Parameters:

  • minValue – [in] Minimum value of the output range.

  • maxValue – [in] Maximum value of the output range.

Returns:

uint32_t The mapped sensor value within the specified range.

bool isAboveThreshold(int threshold)

Checks if the soil moisture level exceeds a threshold.

Compares the current raw sensor value against a specified threshold to determine if the moisture level is above it.

Attention

Requires a prior call to read() to update the sensor value.

Parameters:

threshold – [in] The threshold value for soil moisture (0–1023).

Returns:

bool true if the moisture level is above the threshold, false otherwise.

int getMoisture()

Retrieves the raw analog soil moisture value.

Returns the most recent raw 10-bit analog value (0–1023) read from the sensor.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to read().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

int The raw analog sensor value.

int getMoisturePercentage()

Retrieves the soil moisture as a percentage.

Returns the internally stored percentage value (0–100) computed from the raw analog sensor value.

Attention

Requires a prior successful call to read().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

int The soil moisture as a percentage.

int getAverageReading(int samples = 10)

Computes the average sensor reading over multiple samples.

Takes multiple readings from the sensor with a 10ms delay between each and returns their average to reduce noise.

Attention

Ensure the sensor is connected and samples is a positive integer.

Parameters:

samples – [in] Number of samples to average (default: 10).

Returns:

int The averaged raw sensor value.

void onThresholdCross(int threshold, void (*callback)())

Sets a callback function for threshold-crossing events.

Configures a callback function to be triggered when the soil moisture level crosses the specified threshold, invoking the callback if the threshold is currently exceeded.

Attention

The callback function must be defined, have no parameters, and no return value. Requires a prior call to read() for accurate threshold detection.

Parameters:

  • threshold – [in] The threshold value for triggering the callback (0–1023).

  • callback – [in] The function to call when the threshold is crossed.

class Ultrasonic
#include <ultrasonic.h>

Manages distance measurements using an ultrasonic sensor.

The Ultrasonic class provides functionality for measuring distances with an ultrasonic sensor connected to an Arduino via trigger and echo pins. It supports calculating the echo pulse duration and converting it to distances in centimeters, millimeters, or inches, with configurable timeout settings.

Public Functions

Ultrasonic(uint8_t _triggerPin, uint8_t _echoPin, unsigned long timeOut = 20000UL)

Initializes the Ultrasonic sensor with the specified trigger and echo pins, and sets the timeout value.

This constructor sets up the ultrasonic sensor by assigning the trigger and echo pins and configuring them as output and input respectively. It also sets the timeout for the pulse measurement.

Attention

Ensure that the pin numbers passed are correctly connected to the ultrasonic sensor. The timeout should be set according to the maximum expected distance measurement, default is 23000 microseconds.

Parameters:

  • _triggerPin – [in] The pin number connected to the trigger pin of the ultrasonic sensor.

  • _echoPin – [in] The pin number connected to the echo pin of the ultrasonic sensor.

  • timeOut – [in] The timeout value for the pulse measurement in microseconds.

void read(char unit)

Reads the distance measured by the ultrasonic sensor in the specified unit.

This function reads the time duration from the ultrasonic sensor and converts it to a distance value in centimeters, millimeters, or inches based on the specified unit.

Attention

Ensure that the ultrasonic sensor is properly connected and functioning.

Parameters:

unit – [in] The unit in which the distance is to be measured:

  • ’c’: Centimeters

  • ’m’: Millimeters

  • ’i’: Inches

Returns:

  • The distance measured by the sensor in the specified unit.

  • -1: If an invalid unit is provided.

unsigned int getDistance(char unit)
inline void setTimeout(unsigned long timeOut)

Sets the timeout value for the ultrasonic sensor’s pulse measurement.

This inline function allows you to configure the timeout value, which determines the maximum duration the sensor will wait for the echo signal before timing out.

Attention

Ensure that the timeout value is appropriate for the maximum distance you expect to measure. Setting a very high timeout value can cause delays in the sensor’s responsiveness.

Parameters:

timeOut – [in] The timeout value in microseconds to be set.

Returns:

void

Private Functions

unsigned int duration()

Measures the time duration of the echo received by the ultrasonic sensor.

This function resets the trigger pin, sends a pulse to initiate measurement, and reads the duration of the echo signal received, which corresponds to the distance measured by the ultrasonic sensor.

Attention

Ensure that the trigger pin and echo pin are correctly connected and configured. This function may block for a short period while waiting for the echo signal.

Parameters:

  • None – [in]

  • None – [out]

  • None –

Returns:

  • The duration of the echo signal in microseconds.

class Unit4Relay
#include <unit_4relay.h>

Manages a 4-relay module with I2C interface for relay and LED control.

The Unit4Relay class provides functionality for controlling a 4-relay module over I2C, including initializing the module, setting relay and LED states individually or collectively, switching operating modes (synchronous/asynchronous), and retrieving relay and LED states. It maintains internal state arrays for relays and LEDs.

Public Functions

unit_4relay_error_t begin()

Initializes the Unit 4-Relay module.

Checks for the presence of the module on the I2C bus at address 0x26.

Attention

Ensure the module is powered and connected to the I2C bus before calling.

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Module detected and ready

  • UNIT_4RELAY_ERR_I2C: Module not found or I2C communication error

unit_4relay_error_t init(bool mode)

Configures the operating mode and turns off all relays.

Sets the module to synchronous or asynchronous mode and initializes all relays to OFF.

Attention

Call after begin() to ensure proper initialization.

Parameters:

mode – [in] Operating mode: 

            - `0`: Asynchronous mode

            - `1`: Synchronous mode

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Success

  • UNIT_4RELAY_ERR_INIT: Failed to write initial configuration

unit_4relay_error_t relayWrite(uint8_t number, bool state)

Sets the state of an individual relay.

Turns a specified relay ON or OFF by updating the I2C register and internal state.

Attention

Ensure the relay index is valid (0–3).

Parameters:

  • number – [in] Relay index (0–3).

  • state – [in] Desired state (true for ON, false for OFF).

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Success

  • UNIT_4RELAY_ERR_INDEX: Invalid relay index

unit_4relay_error_t relayAll(bool state)

Sets all relays to the same state.

Turns all relays ON or OFF simultaneously and updates the internal state.

Parameters:

state – [in] Desired state for all relays (true for ON, false for OFF).

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Success

unit_4relay_error_t ledWrite(uint8_t number, bool state)

Sets the state of an individual LED.

Turns a specified indicator LED ON or OFF by updating the I2C register and internal state.

Attention

Ensure the LED index is valid (0–3).

Parameters:

  • number – [in] LED index (0–3).

  • state – [in] Desired state (true for ON, false for OFF).

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Success

  • UNIT_4RELAY_ERR_INDEX: Invalid LED index

unit_4relay_error_t ledAll(bool state)

Sets all LEDs to the same state.

Turns all indicator LEDs ON or OFF simultaneously and updates the internal state.

Parameters:

state – [in] Desired state for all LEDs (true for ON, false for OFF).

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Success

unit_4relay_error_t switchMode(bool mode)

Sets the operating mode of the relay module.

Changes the module’s operating mode to synchronous or asynchronous.

Parameters:

mode – [in] Desired mode (0 for asynchronous, 1 for synchronous).

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Success

int getRelayState(uint8_t number)

Retrieves the state of a specific relay.

Returns the current state of the specified relay from the internal state array.

Attention

Ensure the relay index is valid (0–3).

Parameters:

number – [in] Relay index (0–3).

Returns:

  • 0: Relay is OFF

  • 1: Relay is ON

  • UNIT_4RELAY_ERR_INDEX: Invalid relay index

int getLedState(uint8_t number)

Retrieves the state of a specific LED.

Returns the current state of the specified LED from the internal state array.

Attention

Ensure the LED index is valid (0–3).

Parameters:

number – [in] LED index (0–3).

Returns:

  • 0: LED is OFF

  • 1: LED is ON

  • UNIT_4RELAY_ERR_INDEX: Invalid LED index

unit_4relay_error_t setRelayStates(bool state[4])

Stages relay states without writing to the module.

Updates the internal relay state array with the provided states, deferring physical changes until applyRelayState() is called.

Attention

The state array must contain exactly four elements. Use applyRelayState() to write the staged states to the module.

Parameters:

state – [in] Array of four boolean values representing the desired state for each relay (true for ON, false for OFF).

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Success

unit_4relay_error_t applyRelayState()

Applies the staged relay states to the module.

Writes the internal relay state array to the module’s I2C register, turning relays ON or OFF as specified by the states set via setRelayState().

Attention

Requires a prior call to setRelayState() to stage the desired relay states. Ensure the module is initialized with begin() and init().

Parameters:

None –

Returns:

  • UNIT_4RELAY_OK: Success

  • UNIT_4RELAY_ERR_I2C: I2C communication error

class UsbSwitch
#include <usb_switch.h>

Manages a USB switch module with two PWM-controlled outputs.

The UsbSwitch class provides functionality for controlling a USB switch module with two outputs (USB_OUTPUT1 and USB_OUTPUT2) via PWM-capable pins. It supports setting output values as PWM or percentage, toggling output states, and retrieving current values and statuses. The class maintains internal state for both outputs.

Public Functions

UsbSwitch(uint8_t pin1, uint8_t pin2)

Constructor to initialize the USB Switch module with specified pins.

Configures the provided pins as PWM outputs for controlling USB_OUTPUT1 and USB_OUTPUT2, initializing both outputs to OFF.

Attention

Ensure the pins are PWM-capable and correctly connected to the module.

Parameters:

  • pin1 – [in] The pin controlling USB_OUTPUT1 (yellow wire if using Grove connector).

  • pin2 – [in] The pin controlling USB_OUTPUT2 (white wire if using Grove connector).

void setOutputValue(uint8_t outputNo, int value)

Sets the output value using a PWM value.

Writes a PWM value to the specified output(s), updating the internal status based on whether the value is non-zero.

Attention

Ensure the value is within 0–255 and the output number is valid (0, 1, or 2).

Parameters:

  • outputNo – [in] The output to control (1 for USB_OUTPUT1, 2 for USB_OUTPUT2, 0 for both).

  • value – [in] The PWM value (0–255).

void setOutputValuePercentage(uint8_t outputNo, int percentage)

Sets the output value as a percentage.

Converts a percentage to a PWM value and applies it to the specified output(s), updating the internal status.

Attention

For some devices (e.g., pumping motors), a percentage below 59% may not activate the device.

Parameters:

  • outputNo – [in] The output to control (1 for USB_OUTPUT1, 2 for USB_OUTPUT2, 0 for both).

  • percentage – [in] The output value as a percentage (0–100%).

int getOutputValue(uint8_t outputNo)

Retrieves the current output value.

Reads the current PWM value of the specified output from the pin.

Attention

Ensure the output number is valid (1 or 2).

Parameters:

outputNo – [in] The output to query (1 for USB_OUTPUT1, 2 for USB_OUTPUT2).

Returns:

int The current PWM value (0–255), or 0 if an invalid output is specified.

int getOutputValuePercentage(uint8_t outputNo)

Retrieves the current output value as a percentage.

Converts the current PWM value of the specified output to a percentage.

Attention

Ensure the output number is valid (1 or 2).

Parameters:

outputNo – [in] The output to query (1 for USB_OUTPUT1, 2 for USB_OUTPUT2).

Returns:

int The current output value as a percentage (0–100%), or 0 if an invalid output is specified.

void toggleOutput(uint8_t outputNo)

Toggles the output state between ON and OFF.

Switches the specified output(s) between ON (PWM 255) and OFF (PWM 0), updating the internal status.

Attention

Ensure the output number is valid (0, 1, or 2).

Parameters:

outputNo – [in] The output to toggle (1 for USB_OUTPUT1, 2 for USB_OUTPUT2, 0 for both).

bool getStatus(uint8_t outputNo)

Checks the current status of the output.

Returns whether the specified output is currently ON (non-zero PWM) or OFF.

Attention

Ensure the output number is valid (1 or 2).

Parameters:

outputNo – [in] The output to check (1 for USB_OUTPUT1, 2 for USB_OUTPUT2).

Returns:

bool true if the output is ON, false otherwise or if an invalid output is specified.

bool bspGpioDigitalRead(uint8_t pin)

This function reads the state of a digital pin.

Attention

If the pin isn’t connected to anything, bspGpioDigitalRead() can return either HIGH or LOW (and this can change randomly).

Parameters:

pin – [in] GPIO Pin

Returns:

  • true - HIGH

  • false - LOW

  • Data type: bool

int bspGpioAnalogRead(uint8_t pin)

This function reads the value from the specified analog pin.

Attention

If the analog input pin is not connected to anything, the value returned by bspGpioAnalogRead will fluctuate based on a number of factors (e.g. the values of the other analog inputs, how close your hand is to the board, etc.).

Parameters:

pin – [in] Analog input pin

Returns:

  • The analog reading on the pin. Although it is limited to the resolution of the analog to digital converter * (0-1023 for 10 bits or 0-4095 for 12 bits).

  • Data type: int

void bspGpioAnalogReadResolution(uint8_t bits)

This function sets the size (in bits) of the value returned by bspGpioAnalogRead().

Attention

  • If you set the bspGpioAnalogReadResolution() value to a value higher than your board’s capabilities, the board will only report back at its highest resolution, padding the extra bits with zeros.

  • If you set the bspGpioAnalogReadResolution() value to a value lower than your board’s capabilities, the extra least significant bits read from the ADC will be discarded.

Parameters:

bits – [in] The resolution (in bits). You can set this between 1 and 32.

Returns:

None

void bspGpioAnalogWrite(uint8_t pin, int value)

This function writes an analog value (PWM wave) to a pin.

Parameters:

  • pin – [in] The pin to write to.

  • value – [in] The duty cycle: between 0 (always off) and 255 (always on). Allowed data types: int

Returns:

None

void bspGpioAnalogWriteResolution(uint8_t bits)

This function sets the resolution of the bspGpioAnalogWrite() function. It defaults to 8 bits (values between 0-255).

Attention

  • If you set the bspGpioAnalogWriteResolution() value to a value higher than your board’s capabilities, the board will discard the extra bits.

  • If you set the bspGpioAnalogWriteResolution() value to a value lower than your board’s capabilities, the missing bits will be padded with zeros to fill the hardware required size.

Parameters:

bits – [in] The resolution (in bits). The value can range from 1 to 32.

Returns:

None

unsigned long bspGpioPulseIn(uint8_t pin, uint8_t state, unsigned long timeout)

This function reads a pulse (either HIGH or LOW) on a pin.

Parameters:

  • pin – [in] The pin on which you want to read the pulse. Allowed data types: int.

  • value – [in] Type of pulse to read: either HIGH or LOW. Allowed data types: int.

  • timeout – [in] (optional): The number of microseconds to wait for the pulse to start; default is one second. Allowed data types: unsigned long.

Returns:

  • The length of the pulse (in microseconds) or 0 if no pulse started before the timeout.

  • Data type: unsigned long

unsigned long bspGpioPulseInLong(uint8_t pin, uint8_t state, unsigned long timeout)

This function is an alternative to bspGpioPulseIn() which is better at handling long pulse and interrupt affected scenarios.

Parameters:

  • pin – [in] The pin on which you want to read the pulse. Allowed data types: int.

  • value – [in] Type of pulse to read: either HIGH or LOW. Allowed data types: int.

  • timeout – [in] (optional): The number of microseconds to wait for the pulse to start; default is one second. Allowed data types: unsigned long.

Returns:

  • The length of the pulse (in microseconds) or 0 if no pulse started before the timeout.

  • Data type: unsigned long

uint8_t bspGpioShiftIn(uint8_t dataPin, uint8_t clockPin, uint8_t bitOrder)

This function shifts in a byte of data one bit at a time. Starts from either the most (i.e. the leftmost) or least (rightmost) significant bit. For each bit, the clock pin is pulled high, the next bit is read from the data line, and then the clock pin is taken low.

Parameters:

  • dataPin – [in] The pin on which to input each bit. Allowed data types: int.

  • clockPin – [in] The pin to toggle to signal a read from dataPin.

  • bitOrder – [in] Order to shift in the bits; either MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST. (Most Significant Bit First, or, Least Significant Bit First).

Returns:

  • The value read.

  • Data type: uint8_t

void bspGpioShiftOut(uint8_t dataPin, uint8_t clockPin, uint8_t bitOrder, uint8_t val)

This function shifts out a byte of data one bit at a time. Starts from either the most (i.e. the leftmost) or least (rightmost) significant bit. Each bit is written in turn to a data pin, after which a clock pin is pulsed (taken high, then low) to indicate that the bit is available.

Parameters:

  • dataPin – [in] The pin on which to output each bit. Allowed data types: int.

  • clockPin – [in] The pin to toggle once the dataPin has been set to the correct value. Allowed data types: int.

  • bitOrder – [in] Order to shift out the bits; either MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST. (Most Significant Bit First, or, Least Significant Bit First).

  • val – [in] The data to shift out. Allowed data types: uint8_t.

Returns:

None

void bspGpioTone(uint8_t pin, unsigned int frequency, unsigned long duration)

This function generates a square wave of the specified frequency (and 50% duty cycle) on a pin. A duration can be specified, otherwise the wave continues until a call to bspGpioNoTone().

Parameters:

  • pin – [in] The pin on which to generate the tone.

  • frequency – [in] The frequency of the tone in hertz. Allowed data types: unsigned int.

  • duration – [in] (optional): The duration of the tone in milliseconds . Allowed data types: unsigned long.

Returns:

None

void bspGpioNoTone(uint8_t pin)

This function stops the generation of a square wave triggered by bspGpioTone(). Has no effect if no tone is being generated.

Attention

If you want to play different pitches on multiple pins, you need to call bspGpioNoTone() on one pin before calling bspGpioTone() on the next pin.

Parameters:

pin – [in] The pin on which to stop generating the tone

Returns:

None

bool bspGpioDigitalRead(uint8_t pin)

This function reads the state of a digital pin.

Attention

If the pin isn’t connected to anything, bspGpioDigitalRead() can return either HIGH or LOW (and this can change randomly).

Parameters:

pin – [in] GPIO Pin

Returns:

  • true - HIGH

  • false - LOW

  • Data type: bool

int bspGpioAnalogRead(uint8_t pin)

This function reads the value from the specified analog pin.

Attention

If the analog input pin is not connected to anything, the value returned by bspGpioAnalogRead will fluctuate based on a number of factors (e.g. the values of the other analog inputs, how close your hand is to the board, etc.).

Parameters:

pin – [in] Analog input pin

Returns:

  • The analog reading on the pin. Although it is limited to the resolution of the analog to digital converter * (0-1023 for 10 bits or 0-4095 for 12 bits).

  • Data type: int

void bspGpioAnalogReadResolution(uint8_t bits)

This function sets the size (in bits) of the value returned by bspGpioAnalogRead().

Attention

  • If you set the bspGpioAnalogReadResolution() value to a value higher than your board’s capabilities, the board will only report back at its highest resolution, padding the extra bits with zeros.

  • If you set the bspGpioAnalogReadResolution() value to a value lower than your board’s capabilities, the extra least significant bits read from the ADC will be discarded.

Parameters:

bits – [in] The resolution (in bits). You can set this between 1 and 32.

Returns:

None

void bspGpioAnalogWrite(uint8_t pin, int value)

This function writes an analog value (PWM wave) to a pin.

Parameters:

  • pin – [in] The pin to write to.

  • value – [in] The duty cycle: between 0 (always off) and 255 (always on). Allowed data types: int

Returns:

None

void bspGpioAnalogWriteResolution(uint8_t bits)

This function sets the resolution of the bspGpioAnalogWrite() function. It defaults to 8 bits (values between 0-255).

Attention

  • If you set the bspGpioAnalogWriteResolution() value to a value higher than your board’s capabilities, the board will discard the extra bits.

  • If you set the bspGpioAnalogWriteResolution() value to a value lower than your board’s capabilities, the missing bits will be padded with zeros to fill the hardware required size.

Parameters:

bits – [in] The resolution (in bits). The value can range from 1 to 32.

Returns:

None

unsigned long bspGpioPulseIn(uint8_t pin, uint8_t state, unsigned long timeout = 1000000UL)

This function reads a pulse (either HIGH or LOW) on a pin.

Parameters:

  • pin – [in] The pin on which you want to read the pulse. Allowed data types: int.

  • value – [in] Type of pulse to read: either HIGH or LOW. Allowed data types: int.

  • timeout – [in] (optional): The number of microseconds to wait for the pulse to start; default is one second. Allowed data types: unsigned long.

Returns:

  • The length of the pulse (in microseconds) or 0 if no pulse started before the timeout.

  • Data type: unsigned long

unsigned long bspGpioPulseInLong(uint8_t pin, uint8_t state, unsigned long timeout = 1000000UL)

This function is an alternative to bspGpioPulseIn() which is better at handling long pulse and interrupt affected scenarios.

Parameters:

  • pin – [in] The pin on which you want to read the pulse. Allowed data types: int.

  • value – [in] Type of pulse to read: either HIGH or LOW. Allowed data types: int.

  • timeout – [in] (optional): The number of microseconds to wait for the pulse to start; default is one second. Allowed data types: unsigned long.

Returns:

  • The length of the pulse (in microseconds) or 0 if no pulse started before the timeout.

  • Data type: unsigned long

uint8_t bspGpioShiftIn(uint8_t dataPin, uint8_t clockPin, uint8_t bitOrder)

This function shifts in a byte of data one bit at a time. Starts from either the most (i.e. the leftmost) or least (rightmost) significant bit. For each bit, the clock pin is pulled high, the next bit is read from the data line, and then the clock pin is taken low.

Parameters:

  • dataPin – [in] The pin on which to input each bit. Allowed data types: int.

  • clockPin – [in] The pin to toggle to signal a read from dataPin.

  • bitOrder – [in] Order to shift in the bits; either MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST. (Most Significant Bit First, or, Least Significant Bit First).

Returns:

  • The value read.

  • Data type: uint8_t

void bspGpioShiftOut(uint8_t dataPin, uint8_t clockPin, uint8_t bitOrder, uint8_t val)

This function shifts out a byte of data one bit at a time. Starts from either the most (i.e. the leftmost) or least (rightmost) significant bit. Each bit is written in turn to a data pin, after which a clock pin is pulsed (taken high, then low) to indicate that the bit is available.

Parameters:

  • dataPin – [in] The pin on which to output each bit. Allowed data types: int.

  • clockPin – [in] The pin to toggle once the dataPin has been set to the correct value. Allowed data types: int.

  • bitOrder – [in] Order to shift out the bits; either MSBFIRST or LSBFIRST. (Most Significant Bit First, or, Least Significant Bit First).

  • val – [in] The data to shift out. Allowed data types: uint8_t.

Returns:

None

void bspGpioTone(uint8_t pin, unsigned int frequency, unsigned long duration)

This function generates a square wave of the specified frequency (and 50% duty cycle) on a pin. A duration can be specified, otherwise the wave continues until a call to bspGpioNoTone().

Parameters:

  • pin – [in] The pin on which to generate the tone.

  • frequency – [in] The frequency of the tone in hertz. Allowed data types: unsigned int.

  • duration – [in] (optional): The duration of the tone in milliseconds . Allowed data types: unsigned long.

Returns:

None

void bspGpioNoTone(uint8_t pin)

This function stops the generation of a square wave triggered by bspGpioTone(). Has no effect if no tone is being generated.

Attention

If you want to play different pitches on multiple pins, you need to call bspGpioNoTone() on one pin before calling bspGpioTone() on the next pin.

Parameters:

pin – [in] The pin on which to stop generating the tone

Returns:

None

Reads a single byte using I2C from a register.

This function read a single byte over the I2C interface from a register and stores it in the provided reference variable.

Attention

Ensure that the device is correctly connected and that I2C communication is functioning. The function includes a loop with retries and delays to handle cases where the byte is not immediately available.

Parameters:

  • address – [in] Device’s I2C address

  • reg – [in] The register to read from

  • byte – [out] Reference to a variable where the read byte will be stored.

Returns:

  • BSP_I2C_OK : Success

  • BSP_I2C_ERR_READ: Error reading from the I2C bus.

file utility.cpp
#include “utility.h”

Source file for Utility library. This library provides various utility functions for multiple purposes.

@license This library is released under the MIT License.

Version

0.1.0

Date

2024-11-01

Author

Tuan Nguyen

Functions

void scanI2CDevices()

Scans the I2C bus for connected devices.

The scanI2CDevices function probes the I2C bus for devices by attempting communication with addresses from 1 to 126. It reports detected devices and errors via the Serial interface, providing a summary of the scan results. The function is designed for debugging and identifying I2C device addresses on an Arduino-compatible board.

uint8_t crc8(const uint8_t *data, int len)

Calculates CRC-8 checksum for the given data using SHT40’s polynomial.

This function computes an 8-bit CRC checksum using the polynomial defined in the SHT40 datasheet. It is used to verify data integrity when reading from the SHT40 sensor.

The CRC-8 parameters are:

  • Initialization value: 0xFF

  • Polynomial: 0x31 (x⁸ + x⁵ + x⁴ + 1)

  • No final XOR (0x00)

Example from datasheet: For data bytes {0xBE, 0xEF}, the CRC result is 0x92.

Attention

Ensure that data points to a valid memory location of at least len bytes. This function does not perform bounds checking.

Parameters:

  • data – [in] Pointer to the input data buffer.

  • len – [in] Length of the data buffer in bytes.

Returns:

  • CRC-8 checksum as an 8-bit unsigned integer.

int compareVersion(String v1, String v2)

Compares two firmware version strings.

This function compares two version strings (e.g., “1.0”, “0.9.3”, “2”) by parsing up to three levels of semantic versioning: major, minor, and patch. Missing segments are treated as zero, allowing flexible comparison of version formats like “0.1”, “0.1.0”, or “1”.

Attention

Version strings should be in numeric dot-separated format. Non-numeric parts are ignored. For example, “1.0a” would parse as “1.0.0”. Only the first three segments are considered.

Parameters:

  • v1 – [in] The current firmware version (as a String).

  • v2 – [in] The incoming/target firmware version (as a String).

Returns:

  • -1 if v1 is lower than v2

  • 0 if both versions are equal

  • 1 if v1 is greater than v2

int compareVersion(String v1, String v2)

Compares two firmware version strings.

This function compares two version strings (e.g., “1.0”, “0.9.3”, “2”) by parsing up to three levels of semantic versioning: major, minor, and patch. Missing segments are treated as zero, allowing flexible comparison of version formats like “0.1”, “0.1.0”, or “1”.

Attention

Version strings should be in numeric dot-separated format. Non-numeric parts are ignored. For example, “1.0a” would parse as “1.0.0”. Only the first three segments are considered.

Parameters:

  • v1 – [in] The current firmware version (as a String).

  • v2 – [in] The incoming/target firmware version (as a String).

Returns:

  • -1 if v1 is lower than v2

  • 0 if both versions are equal

  • 1 if v1 is greater than v2

page README

ArduinoJson is a C++ JSON library for Arduino and IoT (Internet Of Things).

page DHT20 Library

Overview

This library provides a set of functions to interface with the DHT20 temperature and humidity sensor. It allows users to initialize the sensor, read temperature and humidity data, and reset the sensor if necessary.

Features

  • Initialize DHT20 Sensor: Ensures the sensor is ready for use.

  • Read Temperature and Humidity: Retrieves accurate temperature and humidity data.

  • Reset Functionality: Allows resetting the sensor if needed.
